description: Storage, LevelDB and chainstate persistence health: volume capacity, per-database read/write latency and hit rate, chainstate flush cost and triggers, block file I/O, pruning, snapshots and optional indexes. The layer every chainstate stall is attributable to.

panels.description: Disk space used and free, stacked so the total volume size is visible as the height of the band.
panels.title: Volume Usage

panels.description: Disk usage as a percentage of the volume. A gauge with thresholds answers 'how much headroom is left' at a glance; a flat line at 50% over seven days does not.
panels.title: Volume Used Percent

panels.description: Mean LevelDB read latency per database. chainstate serves the coins cache, index the block index, and txindex the optional transaction index. Reads here are the ones that missed the cache, so this is the number to watch when a chainstate stall needs explaining.
panels.title: Read Latency by Database

panels.description: Fraction of reads served without touching disk, per database. A falling rate means the working set has outgrown the block cache and reads are going to the table files.
panels.title: Read Hit Rate by Database

panels.description: Mean time to commit a write batch, per database. A rising value here means the write path is becoming the bottleneck rather than read latency.
panels.title: Write Batch Latency

panels.description: Write batches per second against explicit sync writes. Sync writes force a flush to stable storage and are far more expensive, so a sync-write spike explains a latency spike. Read failures should sit at zero.
panels.title: Write Batches & Sync Writes

panels.description: Time to flush the chainstate to disk. This is the main chainstate I/O cost and was only visible in bench logs before instrumentation. Periodic writes should be fast; a FORCE_SYNC during shutdown is legitimately slow.
panels.title: Flush Duration

panels.description: Why the chainstate was flushed, stacked by trigger mode. Modes are discovered dynamically, so a mode that has not fired yet is absent instead of appearing as an empty series. Prune-triggered flushes are scaled up so they are visible next to the per-mode counts.
panels.title: Flush Trigger

panels.description: Number of coins written on the last flush against the dirty count that triggered it. Flush duration scales with this, so read the two panels together.
panels.title: Coins Written per Flush

panels.description: Dynamic memory held by the coins cache when the chainstate was last flushed. This is the input to flush cost: a large dirty cache is what makes a periodic write take as long as it does.
panels.title: Coins Cache Memory at Flush

panels.description: Block file throughput as blocks are read and written. Reads dominate during initial sync and during any reorg replay; writes track new blocks only.
panels.title: Block Read & Write Throughput

panels.description: Mean time to read or write a block file. Rising write latency with flat throughput points at the storage device rather than at load.
panels.title: Block Read & Write Latency

panels.description: Latency of writing the block index and the undo data. The undo file is written for every connected block and is what makes a reorg possible without re-downloading.
panels.title: Index & Undo Write Latency

panels.description: Block file read and write failures, including checksum mismatches. Any non-zero value here means disk corruption or a failing device, not a transient error.
panels.title: Block File Failures

panels.description: Index entries and block files written per second, with undo bytes on the right axis. A byte rate on a count axis was invisible.
panels.title: Index Write Volume

panels.description: Block files actually deleted per second, against the number eligible for pruning. All zero on an unpruned node, which is the normal configuration.
panels.title: Pruning Activity

panels.description: Cost of deciding what to prune and then unlinking it. Both read only block index metadata, not block data. Manual is the explicit -pruneblockchain call.
panels.title: Prune Scan Cost

panels.description: Time to flush an assumeutxo snapshot to disk. Only active while a snapshot is being loaded or validated, so a flat zero line is expected on a node that never does.
panels.title: Snapshot Flush

panels.description: Cost of computing snapshot statistics, in microseconds, with the aborted-snapshot rate on the right axis. The abort rate is almost always zero and was pinned flat against a microsecond-scale cost.
panels.title: Snapshot Stats & Aborts

panels.description: Block height each optional index has reached. A persistent gap behind the chain tip (see the Blocks dashboard) means an index is still syncing or has stalled, which silently disables the RPCs that depend on it.
panels.title: Index Sync Progress

panels.description: Per-block cost of updating the txindex, in microseconds, with the reorg rewind rate on the right axis.
panels.title: Index Block Cost & Reorg Rewinds

title: Storage & Database Health
